title: A Longitudinal Examination of the Relationship Between National-Level Per Capita Advertising Expenditure and National-Level Life Satisfaction Across 76 Countries
authors: Michael A. Wiles; Saeed Janani; Darima Fotheringham; Chadwick J. Miller
eligible_reason: Not a DiD. The regressor of interest is continuous national per capita advertising expenditure (advertising); every main regression (Table 2 models, Table 3 Griffith et al. replication) is xtreg/areg of LifeLadder on advertising with country FE, year dummies and about 23 time-varying country controls (Gini, social support, log GDP, CPI, etc.), plus advertising x moderator interactions. No binary treatment switching on at country-specific dates.
design_notes: Stata Code.do. Country-year panel, 76 countries, 2006-2019 (Data.dta, 874 rows). Estimators: country FE (xtreg fe / areg absorb(ID)) with i.year, random effects comparisons, Gaussian-copula endogeneity term (capula), Granger causality (xtgcause), xtabond2 tests. Paper also has four online/lab experiments (CSV data shipped).

ineligible_specs_listed.reason: continuous treatment (advertising per capita) with time-varying controls and advertising x moderator interactions
replication of Griffith et al.: f.Life on continuous advertising, random effects and FE
appendix; continuous advertising (impressions, media types, by-year slopes, outlier and religion moderators)

data_files: 21-0136 experiment stimuli and data/E1-E4 csv files
data_files_note: Country-year panel assembled from World Happiness Report and public country statistics; advertising expenditure source per paper.
data_provenance_note: Authors' estimation data; no masking or sampling stated.
screener_notes: Screened from package and OpenAlex metadata (no article text). code_prescore 2 is driven by country and year FE; the treatment is continuous and every column has time-varying controls, so no staggered binary design exists.
